claims.label: supported
claims.claim_summary: Jev holds an advantage on new learners, while deep KT leads on unseen items.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: For new learners the advantage holds from their first interactions, whereas on unseen items with all learners logged, deep KT remains ahead.

evidence_spans.source_text: JevKT is above the best deep KT model at every position, already for the second to fifth interactions (.714 vs. .691), when the new learner has shown little evidence, and in 33/35 dataset–position cells (Table 9).
JevKT (.713) and Jev0-shot (.704) stay well above LOKT (.664), but the best deep KT model, trained on all learners and chosen on test, is ahead (.729; JevKT is better on 1/7 datasets; Table 10).

claims.label: supported
claims.claim_summary: Jev0-shot outperforms both LOKT and the top 8-learner deep KT baseline.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: This is above the strongest training-free LLM-KT baseline, LOKT (.671), and above the best deep KT model trained on 8 learners (.689; higher on 5/7 datasets).

evidence_spans.source_text: Without training data, Jev0-shot is above LLM-based KT on all seven datasets and above deep KT trained on 8 learners on average

claims.label: supported
claims.claim_summary: JevKT outperforms deep KT across all datasets at N=8, 16, and 32.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: JevKT is ahead of the best deep KT model by +.033, +.023 and +.016 mean AUC at N=8, 16 and 32 (on 7/7, 7/7 and 7/7 datasets); the mean difference is +.004 at N=64, −.002 at N=128, −.008 at N=256 and −.028 with the full training data.

evidence_spans.source_text: Without training data, Jev0-shot is above LLM-based KT on all seven datasets and above deep KT trained on 8 learners on average; JevKT stays ahead of deep KT up to N=64 on average. Wins: datasets on which Jev beats every baseline in its block.
JevKT leads on average up to N=64 (on 7/7 datasets at N=8 and 4/7 at N=64); the lead shrinks with N and disappears between N=64 and 128 on average, at different N for different datasets.

claims.label: supported
claims.claim_summary: On unseen items, Jev beats LOKT but lags behind fully-trained deep KT.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: JevKT (.713) and Jev0-shot (.704) stay well above LOKT (.664), but the best deep KT model, trained on all learners and chosen on test, is ahead (.729; JevKT is better on 1/7 datasets; Table 10).

evidence_spans.source_text: JevKT is ahead of the best deep KT model only on Junyi; averaged over datasets the gap (.713 vs. .729) is close to the full-data gap of P1, so unseen items do not by themselves favour the System-One model.

claims.label: supported
claims.claim_summary: Similar-learner statistics account for most of JevKT's performance boost at N=16.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: At N=16 the similar-learner statistic alone raises Jev0-shot from .706 to .729, 64 KC-matched shots alone to .724, and both together to .730.

evidence_spans.source_text: Table 6: Input ablation under cold start (N=16 training learners, mean over 5 seeds, same early-window targets as P1). Each row adds one input to the learner’s history; Jev0-shot uses no training learners.

Every form of evidence improves on Jev0-shot (.706), and the similar-learner statistic alone (.729) is almost as good as the full JevKT input (.730). KC-matched shots help less than the statistic (.720 with 16 shots, .724 with 64), and combining the two is sub-additive: the gain over the statistic alone is clear only on DBE-KT22.

claims.label: supported
claims.claim_summary: Reasoning tokens fail to raise Qwen's AUC, whereas single-pass Jev significantly outperforms Thinking-KT.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: A reasoning budget of 1024 or 2048 tokens never improves AUC significantly over the same model without reasoning, while one Jev pass beats Thinking-KT on all seven datasets (Holm-corrected, ∆AUC +.038 to +.073 against the budget of 2048).

evidence_spans.source_text: With full data: thinking does not improve Thinking-KT over no-think at budget 1024 or 2048 (0/7 datasets); one Jev call beats Thinking-KT at either budget (7/7); JevKT beats Jev0-shot (7/7).

Think −No-think: Thinking-KT with reasoning budget 1024 / 2048 minus the same model without reasoning. Jev −Thinking-KT: one Jev call vs. 10 sampled reasoning generations.

claims.label: supported
claims.claim_summary: JevKT delivers single predictions in 325ms at 20% the API cost of Thinking-KT.
claims.claim_text_verbatim: One JevKT prediction takes 325 ms in a single call and costs $886 per million predictions, about 1/5 of Thinking-KT, which needs $4,360 and 41.7 s per prediction even with its ten votes issued in parallel; Jev0-shot costs $44.

evidence_spans.source_text: API costs are the OpenRouter prices we paid. JevKT’s 64 shots make its prompt long, so it costs more than Jev0-shot but still about one fifth of Thinking-KT, and it answers in one call instead of ten.
